description:
How reliably does the agent answer the same question? Per-case pass rates, flaky cases, and an interval that respects repeats.

What it does. Groups evaluations by case_key (or session) and reports each case's pass rate with a Wilson interval, the flaky cases least reliable first, and an overall rate bootstrapped over cases rather than pooled attempts. Deterministic, local, no model call. Full detail: iris://capabilities.

When not to use it. To compare two runs (compare_runs). To score an output (evaluate_output).

Returns. JSON: case_key, group_by, question, cases, attempts, overall, pooled, flaky_cases, by_case, summary.

Errors. IRIS_STORAGE_ERROR. No matching evaluations is cases 0, not an error. Failures return {"error":{code,message,recovery}} with isError; follow recovery.

Siblings. compare_runs — compare two runs against each other; log_trace — record an execution with a case_key; get_traces — read the traces themselves.

case_key.description: narrow to a single case — the fastest way to ask "is this one question flaky?"

group_by.description: case_key (default): repeats of one question; session: the turns of one conversation, so a session answered both ways reads as flaky and by_case rows carry session ids

min_attempts.description: ignore cases asked fewer than this many times (default 1). A case asked once cannot be shown to be flaky

question.description: read the rate for ONE question: only evaluations that judged it count, and an attempt passes when every rule answering it passed — not the composed verdict

run.description: narrow to one run; omit to read every evaluation that carries a case key

session.description: narrow to one session (the turns logged with that session_id)

name: compare_traces
title: Compare Traces
